region: Eastern Hokkaido (Okhotsk coast, Shiretoko, Akan-Mashū, Kushiro)
title: Japan — Hokkaido, Drift Ice and Cranes
subtitle: Walking on sea ice at Utoro, eagles off Rausu, Ainu culture and red-crowned cranes in the Kushiro snow
summary: A 13-day winter expedition through eastern Hokkaido in mid-to-late February: the icebreaker at Abashiri, a dry-suit walk on drift ice at Utoro, Steller's sea eagles at Rausu, steaming caldera lakes at Kussharo and Akan, living Ainu culture at Upopoy and Lake Akan, and wild cranes on the Kushiro plain. It is a cold-weather, self-drive trip with a hotel or minshuku every night.
introduction: In February the Sea of Okhotsk freezes and the ice drifts south onto the Hokkaido coast. On this route you board an icebreaker at Abashiri, then pull on a dry suit at Utoro and walk across the floes with a guide. At Rausu a boat takes you to Steller's sea eagles perched on the ice. Inland, hot springs keep Lake Kussharo open for whooper swans, Lake Akan is frozen hard enough to walk on, and red-crowned cranes dance in the snow at Tsurui. Two days of Ainu culture, at Upopoy and at Akan, frame the trip as a place and a people, not only a landscape.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was desert, tents and a rented vehicle in warm weather. This is the opposite: a frozen sea, steaming volcanic lakes, no camping and nights at -10 to -20 C, with onsen after every cold day. The shared element is a long drive through sparsely populated country.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Most visitors see Hokkaido at the Sapporo Snow Festival or on a ski package around Niseko. This route leaves Sapporo after one day and spends eight nights in the Okhotsk and Kushiro regions, where tour buses rarely stop, and puts the group on the sea ice, not behind a rail.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Distinct from D14 Kyushu, which is volcanoes, onsen and historic towns in the warm south: here the draw is sea ice, wildlife and Ainu heritage in deep winter, and the season and the ice give it a hard deadline. It is also among the most expensive options in the portfolio.

coordinates.label: Eastern Hokkaido, between Abashiri and Kushiro

duration.note: Day 1 departs Paris; day 2 arrives New Chitose; day 13 flies home from Haneda. Domestic flights on days 4 and 12.

recommendedTravelWindow.window: About 12–24 February 2027 (second half of February for the best chance of drift ice)
recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Drift ice usually arrives in late January and leaves by early April, and the second half of February is typically the best period. The Sapporo Snow Festival (4–11 February 2027) ends before this window, which also avoids its hotel prices and crowds. Lunar New Year (6 February) travel has ended by departure.

februarySuitability.summary: Peak drift ice, Rausu cruises still running, cranes at feeding sites, Sounkyo ice festival on. Very cold (night -10 to -25 C inland) and short daylight.

marchSuitability.summary: Drift ice is retreating and Rausu cruises usually end in early March; Upopoy is closed 27 February – 8 March. Milder and quieter, with cranes still being fed to late March. A good fallback only if the ice has stayed late.

climate.regionNote: Ranges are typical planning ranges for the Okhotsk coast and Kushiro plain, not a forecast and not read from JMA tables in this research; inland sites such as Tsurui and Kussharo are several degrees colder at night than the coast.

february.rainfall: Dry, powdery snow; some snowfall most days on the Okhotsk side, Kushiro is sunnier
february.notes: Strong winds can cause whiteouts and road closures; the east is colder but usually less snowy than Sapporo.

march.rainfall: Snow with some wet days late in the month
march.notes: Thaw begins; roads are wetter and ice is melting from the coast.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Route 334 over Shiretoko Pass is closed from about November to April, so Utoro and Rausu are linked only by a long detour. Main roads are ploughed; side roads can close in storms.
climate.seaConditions: The Okhotsk Sea is covered in drift ice from late January to early April. Ice cover varies strongly from year to year and from day to day; wind can push it away from the coast.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Steller's sea eagles and white-tailed eagles on the ice near Rausu (late January to early March), red-crowned cranes fed at Tsurui from mid/late November to late March, whooper swans at Lake Kussharo, yezo deer on roads. Bears normally hibernate in mid-winter.

climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Fares seen from Paris to Sapporo cover 2 February to 20 March 2027 at about EUR 1,045–1,296; festival and Lunar New Year weeks are dearer.

geography.summary: The Okhotsk coast of Hokkaido, the Shiretoko peninsula, the Akan-Mashū caldera lakes and the Kushiro Marsh, in one 600-km loop.
geography.distinctive: Drift ice from the Amur River reaches lower latitudes here than anywhere else in the world, making Hokkaido the southernmost seasonal sea-ice coast in the Northern Hemisphere.

landscapes.name: Okhotsk drift-ice coast
landscapes.description: Sea ice stretching to the horizon from Abashiri to Rausu, with Shiretoko's volcanic ridge behind.

landscapes.name: Lake Kussharo and Lake Mashū
landscapes.description: Two caldera lakes: Kussharo frozen with thermal open patches, Mashū a crater lake with steep walls.

landscapes.name: Lake Akan
landscapes.description: Frozen lake beneath volcanic cones, with geothermal baths along its south shore.

landscapes.name: Kushiro Marsh
landscapes.description: Japan's largest wetland, a flat expanse of reeds and rivers in winter.

landscapes.name: Atosanupuri (Mt Iō) vents
landscapes.description: Steaming sulphur vents at Kussharo's shore that stay green and yellow through the snow.

culture.summary: Ainu culture is the cultural core: Upopoy near Sapporo and the Akan Ainu Kotan village, plus Okhotsk fishing towns, markets and local food.

culturalHighlights.name: Upopoy National Ainu Museum and Park, Shiraoi
culturalHighlights.description: Japan's national museum of Ainu history and culture beside Lake Poroto, with exhibitions, cultural demonstrations and a park; open 9:00–17:00, closed Mondays and 27 February – 8 March.

culturalHighlights.name: Akan Ainu Kotan, Lake Akan
culturalHighlights.description: Craft shops, woodcarving and the Ikor theatre on Lake Akan's south shore. Buy from Ainu-run shops and ask first before photographing people.

culturalHighlights.name: Okhotsk fishing towns: Abashiri, Rausu
culturalHighlights.description: Fish markets, the Abashiri Drift Ice Museum and harbour-side restaurants show how the ice shapes the economy.

culturalHighlights.name: Kushiro Washo Market and the Kushiro waterfront
culturalHighlights.description: The place to eat local seafood on the last night in Kushiro.

adventureHighlights.name: Drift-ice walking at Utoro
adventureHighlights.description: Two-hour guided walk on floes in a dry suit, with a guide who reads the ice; cancelled if the ice is thin or moving.

adventureHighlights.name: Winter self-drive across eastern Hokkaido
adventureHighlights.description: About 1,100 km on snow-packed roads with studless tyres, black ice, whiteouts and deer; two licence holders share the driving.

adventureHighlights.name: Snowshoeing on Lake Akan or Kushiro Marsh
adventureHighlights.description: Guided snowshoe walks over a frozen lake or wetland, a few hours at a time.

signatureExperiences.title: Walking on drift ice in a dry suit at Utoro
signatureExperiences.description: A guided walk across the floes in a buoyant dry suit; if the ice is thin the tour becomes more swimming than walking.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The ice has travelled from the Amur River mouth; Hokkaido is the lowest-latitude place where people can walk on seasonal sea ice.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book the evening before through the hotel or an operator in Utoro, for the afternoon or morning; wear a thermal layer under the suit. Allow a spare day (day 11 is flexible).

signatureExperiences.title: Steller's sea eagles by boat off Rausu
signatureExperiences.description: A one- to two-hour cruise through the ice to eagles resting on floes.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Rausu is the only port on the peninsula that runs drift-ice cruises, and the eagles winter here from Siberia.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Reserve a morning departure at least a week ahead; weather and ice conditions decide each day.
signatureExperiences.costNote: From about 5,000 JPY for 1 h; longer cruises cost 9,000–12,000 JPY.

signatureExperiences.title: Red-crowned cranes at Tsurui
signatureExperiences.description: Cranes gather at the Tsurui-Ito Tancho Sanctuary and other feeding sites, standing on snow and displaying in the cold.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Japan's tancho crane, nearly lost in the 1920s, is a cultural symbol; this is where wild birds can be watched from a short distance.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Drive from Lake Akan (about 1.5 h). Go in the early morning for flight and display, and keep to the marked viewing areas. Entry is free or cheap, but confirm.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Free according to a directory listing (unconfirmed); donations welcome.

signatureExperiences.title: Ainu culture at Upopoy and Lake Akan
signatureExperiences.description: A day at the national Ainu museum at Shiraoi, then craft shops and theatre at Akan Ainu Kotan.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Two complementary experiences, one national and institutional, one a community that still lives and trades at the lake.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Upopoy by JR limited express from Sapporo (about 1 h 15) on day 3, not Monday. Akan Kotan on day 9; confirm theatre times locally.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Upopoy ticket not confirmed (old figure about 1,200 JPY); Kotan entry and craft purchases extra.

travelStyle.summary: Rail and flights to get to eastern Hokkaido, then a rental car for the loop from Memanbetsu to Kushiro, with guided activities on the ice.

transport.summary: Trains and a domestic flight reach eastern Hokkaido; a 4WD rental car links the sites, which are spread over 600 km and poorly served by buses in winter.

modes.description: CDG to New Chitose (via Tokyo or another hub), domestic CTS–Memanbetsu (about 1 h) and Kushiro–Haneda.
Airport to Sapporo and Sapporo to Shiraoi for Upopoy. The Senmo Line serves Abashiri and Shiretoko-Shari, with winter tourist trains; timetable to be checked.
Memanbetsu pick-up and Kushiro drop-off with studless tyres, 4WD, car navigation in English.

modes.mode: Alternative: bus, taxi and guided transfers
modes.description: Possible between towns but slow and infrequent in winter; a driver-guide day on the drift-ice section is the fallback if the drivers are not confident.

transport.carRental: Major Japanese chains (Toyota, Nippon, Times, JR Hokkaido, Budget) have counters at Memanbetsu and Kushiro. Winter cars have studless tyres included. One-way drop-off outside Sapporo, Chitose, Asahikawa and Obihiro adds a fee (about 5,400–10,000 JPY elsewhere in Hokkaido; Memanbetsu to Kushiro is not listed). Book early for 4 adults plus luggage.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is legal and common, but winter driving needs care: black ice, whiteouts, left-hand traffic and deer. Two of the four drive; the other two navigate.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Japan accepts only 1949 Geneva Convention IDPs; 1968 Vienna permits are not valid. Licences from France, Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Monaco and Taiwan are not covered by an IDP and instead need an official Japanese translation (for French licences from JAF, applied for online, about 2–3 business days). Apply before departure; the exact route depends on the licence-issuing country.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: The IDP or translation must be carried with the original licence. Foreign licences stop being valid after one year in Japan. Rental firms refuse drivers without the right document.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Not relevant: no motorcycles or scooters in winter.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Self-drive with two drivers, short days (under about 4 h at the wheel), daylight driving only, and a fallback to taxis, JR or a driver-guide if conditions are bad. Leave extra time on days 6 and 7, when the Shiretoko Pass closure forces a long detour.

accommodation.summary: Business hotels in Sapporo, Abashiri and Kushiro; minshuku, ryokan and pension in Utoro, Rausu, Kawayu and Lake Akan, often with onsen and dinner included.

camping.summary: Hokkaido campsites are closed in winter and nights fall to -10 to -25 C. No camping is planned; the trip uses guesthouses and ryokan instead.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Mostly short outdoor sessions on flat ground. The challenge is the cold: layers, insulated boots and hand warmers. The drift-ice walk requires basic fitness and the ability to swim in a dry suit.

itinerary.summary: Thirteen days: fly in, Sapporo and Upopoy, fly to Memanbetsu, drive the Okhotsk coast to Rausu, cross to Kussharo and Akan, see cranes, end in Kushiro, fly out via Haneda.

security.summary: Japan has the lowest advisory level at each authority reviewed: no regional restriction on Hokkaido, no conflict or kidnapping risk. The relevant hazards are natural: severe winter weather, earthquakes and tsunami, plus bears (normally hibernating in February) and off-piste avalanches, which the plan avoids.
security.assessedRoute: New Chitose, Sapporo, Shiraoi, Memanbetsu, Abashiri, Utoro, Rausu, Kawayu (Lake Kussharo), Lake Mashū, Lake Akan, Tsurui, Kushiro, Kushiro Airport, Tokyo Haneda.

advisories.routeImpact: None on the route; the plan has no off-piste skiing and is in winter when bears hibernate.

conflictRisk.note: No conflict advisories for Hokkaido; the UK notes that North Korean missile launches toward Japan occur and tensions can change quickly. Follow Japanese government alerts.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO: no recent history of terrorism in Japan, though attacks cannot be ruled out.

regionalRestrictions: Route 334 over Shiretoko Pass is closed in winter.
Drift-ice tours and cruises depend on ice, wind and operator judgement and can be cancelled at short notice.
Do not leave marked areas on lake ice or drift ice without a licensed guide.
ordinaryRisks: Black ice and whiteouts when driving; deer on the roads at dusk
Extreme cold: frostbite and hypothermia if stranded
Earthquake and tsunami: know the evacuation signs
Off-piste skiing and backcountry avalanches cause deaths each year in Hokkaido (not planned)
Strict drug laws; tattoos can bar entry to some onsen
security.medicalAccess: High-quality hospitals in Sapporo, Abashiri and Kushiro; small towns have clinics only and limited English. The Japan Visitor Hotline (+81 50 3816 2787) offers English help.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Check cover for ice-floe walking, snowshoeing, car excess and natural disasters; most policies exclude off-piste.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; re-check road closures, drift-ice conditions and any earthquake or Middle East airspace disruption in the week before departure.

practicalRequirements.visa: Depends on nationality: UK nationals receive a visa on arrival for up to 90 days (FCDO). Check the Japanese embassy for each passport.
practicalRequirements.entry: Passport with a blank page; return ticket; cash-based economy outside big cities. Meat products cannot be brought in without permission.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: Valid for the whole stay (UK guidance), with a blank page.
permits: No permits for the planned activities.
practicalRequirements.insurance: Winter-activity cover including ice-floe walking, plus rental-car excess; no off-piste.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Good mobile coverage in towns; weaker in Shiretoko and on remote roads. Buy an eSIM or SIM before travel.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards are accepted in cities and bigger hotels, but small minshuku, markets and tour operators often take cash only. Withdraw yen at convenience-store ATMs.
practicalRequirements.medical: Routine vaccinations; no special requirement. Pack medication in original packaging.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Petrol stations are plentiful but can be far apart; keep the tank above half in winter.
equipment: Insulated waterproof boots with grippy soles
Thermal base layers, down jacket, hat, gloves, face cover

advantages: Sea ice, eagles, cranes and Ainu culture are specific to this region and season.
Guided activities are well established and no technical skills are required.
Hot springs after cold days; safe, orderly country with good medical care.
Japan's advisory level is among the lowest of all destinations in the portfolio.
